samples.summary: `GET /start` is single-use and method-agnostic, so any duplicate/speculative request silently breaks the login for 30s
samples.evidence: `if (startConsumed) { res.writeHead(410) … }` at login.ts:272-276 marks the redirect consumed on the *first* request of any kind, before the browser has necessarily navigated. Real, non-adversarial duplicates exist: (a) a HEAD/preview/URL-scanner request (the handler never checks `req.method`, so HEAD consumes it), (b) omnibox/link prefetch when the user copy-pastes the printed `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/start` — the very headless path the comment at login.ts:52-65 says must keep working, (c) the user reloading or hitting Back and retrying after a hiccup, (d) a browser launcher that issues the URL twice. In all of these the real navigation gets `410 START_CONSUMED_MESSAGE`, no `/callback` ever arrives, and the CLI blocks the full 30s (login.ts:373-385) before failing with the generic `Login timed out` — with no hint that the one-time link was burnt. The previous code passed the authorize URL directly to `open()` and had no such failure mode, so this is a newly introduced hang/regression on ordinary paths.

samples.summary: `sawUnboundCallback` lets any local process (or visited page) control the CLI's final error message, producing a false version-skew report
samples.evidence: `sawUnboundCallback` is set at login.ts:309-310 by *any* `GET /callback?code=…` with no `state`, which the surrounding comment itself notes is 'reachable by any local process or visited page'. The timeout then reports `UNBOUND_CALLBACK_MESSAGE` (login.ts:378-380) instead of 'Login timed out'. So a stray/hostile nonce-less request during an otherwise ordinary timeout (browser never finished, network hiccup) makes the CLI assert the *server* is out of date and instruct the user to re-run with `--allow-unbound-callback` — the exact downgrade steer the comment at login.ts:298-305 claims to have closed; it is merely deferred to the timeout. The error is factually wrong on a path where the server is perfectly current.

samples.summary: Unvalidated `--server` value is now written into a response header; an invalid character throws inside the request handler and crashes the process
samples.evidence: `res.writeHead(302, { Location: authorizeUrl })` (login.ts:278) writes `${server}/auth/github?…` where `server` comes straight from `--server`/`WAFFLEBASE_SERVER` with only a trailing-slash strip (login.ts:25; `--server <url>` is declared at commands/root.ts:64 with no validation). Node throws `ERR_INVALID_CHAR` synchronously for a header value containing CR/LF or other invalid chars; the throw happens inside the `createServer` request listener, which has no try/catch, so it surfaces as an uncaught exception outside `runCli`'s envelope (cli.ts:75-91) and kills the CLI instead of producing the `{ error: … }` envelope. Before this delta the `server` string was only printed and handed to `open()`, so it never reached a header.

samples.summary: Legitimate old-server logins now hang for the full 30s instead of failing fast
samples.evidence: The nonce-less branch (login.ts:306-317) no longer settles the callback promise; against a pre-`cliState` backend — the case `UNBOUND_CALLBACK_MESSAGE` exists for — the CLI now blocks 30 seconds before reporting the same message that was previously immediate. The tradeoff is documented, but the cost is a real 30s stall on a supported configuration, and the printed warning ('Still waiting for the browser.') is misleading there because no further callback will ever arrive.

finding.summary: `GET /start` is single-use and method-agnostic, so any duplicate/speculative request silently breaks the login for 30s
finding.evidence: `if (startConsumed) { res.writeHead(410) … }` at login.ts:272-276 marks the redirect consumed on the *first* request of any kind, before the browser has necessarily navigated. Real, non-adversarial duplicates exist: (a) a HEAD/preview/URL-scanner request (the handler never checks `req.method`, so HEAD consumes it), (b) omnibox/link prefetch when the user copy-pastes the printed `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/start` — the very headless path the comment at login.ts:52-65 says must keep working, (c) the user reloading or hitting Back and retrying after a hiccup, (d) a browser launcher that issues the URL twice. In all of these the real navigation gets `410 START_CONSUMED_MESSAGE`, no `/callback` ever arrives, and the CLI blocks the full 30s (login.ts:373-385) before failing with the generic `Login timed out` — with no hint that the one-time link was burnt. The previous code passed the authorize URL directly to `open()` and had no such failure mode, so this is a newly introduced hang/regression on ordinary paths.

verdict.reason: The claimed code is present exactly as described. login.ts:266-281 handles `/start` keyed only on pathname — `req` is read only for `req.url` (line 262), never `req.method` — and sets `startConsumed = true` at line 277 on the first request of any verb, so a HEAD, prefetch, reload, or double-launch burns the one-time redirect and the real navigation receives `410 START_CONSUMED_MESSAGE` (lines 272-276). The printed URL at login.ts:67-68 is that same one-time `startUrl` (line 399), which the comment at lines 52-65 says must serve the headless copy-paste path, so an ordinary reload/retry is a realistic trigger. Once consumed, no `/callback` arrives, the awaited `waitForCallback()` (lines 80, 403) stays pending for the full 30s timeout at lines 373-385, and rejects with the generic 'Login timed out' message (line 380) — the only special-cased timeout message is `sawUnboundCallback`, so there is no consumption-aware signal in the terminal. The sole caller (lines 47-50) provides no retry or re-arm; `setAuthorizeUrl` (lines 400-402) cannot reset `startConsumed`. No guard makes this unreachable, and a hang plus misleading error on a core flow is squarely correctness. Only inaccuracy in the finding is that the browser does show a hint via START_CONSUMED_MESSAGE (line 229-230); the CLI does not, so the substance holds.

finding.summary: `sawUnboundCallback` lets any local process (or visited page) control the CLI's final error message, producing a false version-skew report
finding.evidence: `sawUnboundCallback` is set at login.ts:309-310 by *any* `GET /callback?code=…` with no `state`, which the surrounding comment itself notes is 'reachable by any local process or visited page'. The timeout then reports `UNBOUND_CALLBACK_MESSAGE` (login.ts:378-380) instead of 'Login timed out'. So a stray/hostile nonce-less request during an otherwise ordinary timeout (browser never finished, network hiccup) makes the CLI assert the *server* is out of date and instruct the user to re-run with `--allow-unbound-callback` — the exact downgrade steer the comment at login.ts:298-305 claims to have closed; it is merely deferred to the timeout. The error is factually wrong on a path where the server is perfectly current.

verdict.reason: Verified in the repository: `sawUnboundCallback` is set at packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:309-310 by any unauthenticated `GET /callback?code=…` lacking `state` on the loopback listener, and the 30s timeout at login.ts:373-385 substitutes UNBOUND_CALLBACK_MESSAGE (login.ts:222-226) for 'Login timed out'. Nothing distinguishes a genuinely version-skewed server from a stray or hostile local/visited-page request, so an ordinary timeout preceded by one nonce-less hit reports a false version-skew diagnosis and instructs the user to re-run with `--allow-unbound-callback` — the same downgrade steer the comment at login.ts:298-305 claims to avoid, merely deferred. The design docs (docs/design/cli.md:225-237, docs/design/rest-api.md:380) endorse the deferral but assume the only source of a nonce-less callback is an old server, an assumption the code's own comment contradicts; documented intent is not a guard. No refutation ground holds: the code is present as described, the path is reachable without any bypassing guard, and the consequence (user acting on a false diagnosis to disable the nonce binding) is a real behavioral outcome within the correctness lane, not merely cosmetic text.

finding.summary: The URL printed for copy-paste omits `cliState`, so copying it makes the login fail with a misleading "upgrade the server" message
finding.evidence: login.ts:71-76 builds `oauthUrl` with `&cliState=<nonce>` but prints `${server}/auth/github?mode=cli&port=${port}` — the nonce-less form. If the user visits that printed URL (docs/design/cli.md:176 still documents step 3 as "also prints URL for copy-paste in headless environments"), the backend guard receives `cliState === undefined`, `normalizeCliState` returns undefined, `createState(mode, port, undefined)` stores a nonce-less flow, and auth.controller.ts:130-134 redirects to `127.0.0.1:<port>/callback?code=…` with NO `state`. The CLI's listener then takes the `received === null && !options.allowUnbound` branch (login.ts:263) and REJECTS the login with UNBOUND_CALLBACK_MESSAGE, which tells the user to "Upgrade the server, or re-run with --allow-unbound-callback" — a false diagnosis, since the server is fine and the real cause is that the CLI printed a URL it will not accept the callback for. The login is settled, so it cannot recover.

verdict.reason: The finding's core evidence does not exist in the code. login.ts:66-68 prints `startUrl` (`http://127.0.0.1:<port>/start`, constructed at login.ts:399), not `${server}/auth/github?mode=cli&port=${port}`; grep shows the only `/auth/github?mode=cli` string in CLI source is inside `buildAuthorizeUrl` (login.ts:209-212), which unconditionally appends `&cliState=`. The printed `/start` URL 302-redirects to that same nonce-carrying authorize URL (login.ts:266-281), so the copy-paste path uses a URL that carries the nonce. The claim's second premise is also false: the `received === null && !options.allowUnbound` branch (login.ts:306-317) returns 400, warns once, and keeps waiting without settling; UNBOUND_CALLBACK_MESSAGE is only thrown at the 30s timeout (login.ts:373-385), so the login is not settled/unrecoverable as described. Docs (docs/design/cli.md:175-177) match the implementation.

finding.summary: The usable OAuth URL is now printed only when `open()` throws, so a headless/no-browser environment can be left with no way to continue
finding.evidence: The old code printed the full URL unconditionally plus "If the browser does not open, visit the URL above."; the new code prints the full URL only inside `catch` around `await open(oauthUrl)` (login.ts:78-87). `open()` with the default `wait: false` resolves as soon as the child is spawned and does not reject when the spawned handler (e.g. `xdg-open` under SSH/WSL/headless) fails to surface a browser — and a later child `error` event is not routed to this promise at all. In those cases nothing prints the nonce-carrying URL, and the login dies on the 30-second timeout with "Login timed out", while the only URL the user was shown (line 75) is the nonce-less one that cannot complete the flow (see the previous finding).

verdict.reason: The claimed code shape is not in the repository. The finding says the usable URL is printed only inside the `catch` around `open()` and that the unconditionally printed URL is nonce-less/unusable. In fact login.ts:67-68 print `Opening browser: ${startUrl}` AND `If the browser does not open, visit the URL above.` unconditionally, outside any try/catch; the catch at login.ts:73-75 prints no URL at all, only 'Could not open a browser automatically.'. The printed `startUrl` is the exact same string passed to `open(startUrl)` at login.ts:72, and it is functional: `startUrl` is `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/start` (login.ts:399) and the `/start` handler 302-redirects to the nonce-carrying authorize URL (login.ts:266-281), which was registered via `setAuthorizeUrl(...)` at login.ts:66 before any output, so the `authorizeUrl === null` 503 branch cannot fire. Hence even if `open()` resolves without surfacing a browser (true of `wait: false`), the headless user has already been shown a working, nonce-completing URL plus the copy-paste instruction. No such thing as the described "no way to continue" state exists on this path.

finding.summary: New `callbackReject` on a nonce-less callback can fire before any handler is attached, turning an actionable failure into an unhandled-rejection crash
finding.evidence: `callbackPromise` (login.ts:235) gets no handler until the action reaches `await waitForCallback()` at line 92, which is after `await import('open')` and `await open(oauthUrl)`. The new branch at login.ts:263-271 rejects that promise from the HTTP handler. Any `GET /callback?code=…` without `state` arriving during that window — trivially producible by any other local process racing the loopback port, and possible for a fast browser leg — rejects an unhandled promise, so Node terminates the process with ERR_UNHANDLED_REJECTION instead of emitting UNBOUND_CALLBACK_MESSAGE through `runCli`'s error envelope. The pre-existing timeout rejection could not hit this window (30 s), so the race is introduced by this change.

verdict.reason: The finding's premise is factually absent from the code. The nonce-less callback branch (login.ts:306-317) does not call `callbackReject` at all — it writes a 400 with UNBOUND_CALLBACK_MESSAGE, sets `sawUnboundCallback`, warns once, and returns, intentionally leaving the login waiting (rationale in the comment at 298-305). A grep for `callbackReject(` across packages/cli finds exactly one call site: the 30 s timeout at login.ts:373-385. The HTTP handler's only settle path is `callbackResolve(code)` at login.ts:369. So no rejection can originate from a `GET /callback?code=…` without `state`, and the described unhandled-rejection race has no source. Independently, the pre-await window is already guarded: login.ts:251-259 attaches `callbackPromise.catch(() => {})` immediately at construction, with a comment naming exactly the `await import('open')` / `open()` window the finding cites, while `waitForCallback()` (login.ts:403) returns the original promise so a later `await` still receives the error. Both behaviors are pinned by tests at test/login-callback.test.ts:92-119 ('refuses a callback with no nonce without ending the login', asserting waitForCallback stays unsettled) and :121-134 ('does not crash when a callback arrives before anyone awaits it').
